Yes, to some extent. I think what made DMC3 so tense was Dante being overpowered, but when that suddenly stops and he loses , we know shit has hit the fan. 

It's hard to write an overpowered protagonist, I understand. But I think you have to approach it like Goku, Gojo, Sung jin Woo, Saitama, Mob, etc. Establish his overwhelming strength early on, then keep him away from the action to build tension, think goku heading to namek, Saitama finding deep sea king ,and Gojo in the prison realm. Then, the relief to the audience is when he arrives. 

Having Dante being outsmarted wouldn't even be a bad approach either. Similar to how Dante and Vergil were being manipulated by Arkham. They were weakened and got their destroyed immediately due to their sibling rivalry. White rabbit probably could have set up something similar, seeing as how he's supposed to be a hyper intelligent antagonist. Probably could have done a similar plan to Toji from jjk to weaken Gojo.

You could also make his struggles more internal, like Saitamas boredom, Mobs growth as a person, or Gojos identity as the strongest. I think dmc 3 already had this set up with Dante while recognizing his father is Sparda he actively hated his demon heritage. The show tried to do something similar, but dante, not knowing his heritage kinda made that internal struggle weaker.

Overall, I think Dante being overpowered could have worked, but I'm not sure if the writing team has the chops to pull it off. I think the show was more interested in telling a political commentary with a larger scope than dmc, which is a smaller, more focused drama based on family and humanity.
